status.en: 27 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 29% more than the week before, most of them in Damascus, Aleppo and Quneitra.
status.nb: 27 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 29 prosent flere enn uken før, flest i Damascus, Aleppo og Quneitra.

summary.en: Israeli drones intensified attacks near the Syria‑Lebanon border, wounding six people in Lebanon and striking a Syrian operative linked to Iran as well as a Syrian "terrorist" operating along the border. Syrian security forces dismantled an ISIS cell in Homs province and stepped up operations against former regime loyalists, while ethnic fighting erupted in Hasaka between Kurds and Arabs. Damascus condemned Houthi attacks on Riyadh airport and backed Saudi security, and the UN Security Council reaffirmed Syria's sovereignty. Prospects for a thaw in Polish‑Syrian relations and an expansion of the Abraham Accords were discussed. The conflict caused 2,732 battle‑related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Israels droner intensiverte angrep nær grensen mellom Syria og Libanon, og såret seks personer i Libanon samt rammet en syrisk operativ knyttet til Iran og en syrisk «terrorist» som opererte langs grensen. Syriske sikkerhetsstyrker demonterte en IS‑celle i Homs provins og økte operasjonene mot tidligere regjeringslojalister, mens etnisk vold brøt ut i Hasaka mellom kurdere og arabere. Damaskus fordømte Houthi‑angrepene på Riyadh flyplass og støttet saudisk sikkerhet, og FNs sikkerhetsråd bekreftet Syriens suverenitet. Mulighetene for en oppvarming av de polsk‑syriske forholdene og en utvidelse av Abraham‑avtalene ble diskutert. Konflikten forårsaket 2 732 dødsfall i kamprelaterte handlinger i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Aftermath of the Syrian civil war
background.extract: Disputes and clashes in Syria have continued following the fall of the Assad regime in December 2024, which many sources consider the end of the Syrian civil war. Numerous actors are involved, including clashes between the newly-formed Syrian caretaker government and later the Syrian transitional government led by the former emir of Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham (HTS) and incumbent president Ahmed al-Sharaa, Assad loyalists, Alawite groups, and Druze insurgents; clashes between elements of the Turkish-backed Syrian National Army (SNA) and the government on one side, and formerly the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) on the other; as well as an Israeli invasion and occupation of the demilitarized buffer zone in southwestern Syria.
